entities.name: Construction of Prambanan, the largest Hindu temple in Southeast Asia
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Prambanan Temple Compounds in Central Java, Indonesia — constructed c. 850 CE by the Hindu Mataram Kingdom (specifically attributed to King Rakai Pikatan or his successor Lokapala) — is the largest Hindu temple complex in Indonesia and one of the greatest Hindu temples in Southeast Asia, dedicated to the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva) with the central Shiva temple rising 47 meters, making it one of the tallest Hindu temples ever built. UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991.

Prambanan's construction represented the assertion of Hindu political and religious power in Java at a time when both Hindu and Buddhist kingdoms competed for dominance: the Mataram Hindu dynasty built Prambanan partly in response to the Buddhist Sailendra dynasty's Borobudur (completed c. 825 CE). The complex originally consisted of 240 temples; the Shiva Mahadeva temple at its center is a masterpiece of Hindu temple architecture, with the Ramayana reliefs on its balustrade (totaling 1,500 relief panels across the compound) constituting one of the most extensive Ramayana narrative sculptures in the world.

Prambanan was abandoned after a volcanic eruption and earthquake c. 930 CE caused the Mataram court to move east, and the temples collapsed over centuries (a major earthquake in 1549 toppled most spires). Dutch colonial reconstruction began in 1918; modern UNESCO-supported restoration continues. The 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake caused additional damage. Prambanan today remains an active Hindu temple and pilgrimage site for the small Balinese Hindu community and for Javanese visitors, while also being one of Indonesia's most visited tourist sites.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Prambanan — the largest Hindu temple complex in Indonesia, a theological and political monument rivaling Buddhist Borobudur, containing one of the world's most extensive Ramayana relief sculptures, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — is Southeast Asia's greatest Hindu architectural achievement.
